chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Kuleyb ibn Muawiya, who said:

Abu Baseer and his companions were drinking Al-Nabeez, breaking it with water. So I narrated that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'And how did the water make permissible the intoxicant? Tell them not to drink from it, neither a little nor a lot.' I said: 'They mention that the approval of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) makes it permissible for them.' He said: 'And how could the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) permit the intoxicant, while they do not drink from it, neither a little nor a lot? Refrain from drinking it.'

So we gathered in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abu Baseer said to him: 'They have come to us from you with such and such.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'True, O Abu Muhammad! The water does not make permissible the intoxicant, therefore do not drink from it, neither a little nor a lot.'

key_terms.آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him)
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Al-Nabeez (a specific type of fermented drink made from dates or raisins)
key_terms.يَكْسِرُونَهُ: They break it (referring to diluting or reducing its strength)

ai.seo_question: Does adding water make fermented drinks like Al-Nabeez permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the juristic debate regarding Al-Nabeez, refuting the view that dilution with water renders an intoxicant permissible. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'Qalilan wa Katheeran' (little or much), asserting that the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him) abstained from it entirely, thereby setting a precedent for complete avoidance rather than conditional permissibility. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the consistency of the Imams' practice as a source of legal derivation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahy, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Kuleyb Bin Muawiya who said,

‘Abu Baseer and his companions were drinking Al Nabeez, breaking it with the water. So I discussed that with Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws said to me: ‘And how can the water make Permissible the Prohibited intoxicant. Do not be drinking from it, neither a little nor a lot’. I said, ‘They are mentioning that the approval of the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww makes it Permissible for them’. So heasws said: ‘And how could the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww have Permitted the intoxicant, and theyasws are not drinking from it, neither a little nor a lot? Refrain from drinking it’.

So we gathered in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Abu Baseer said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They have come to us from you<sup>asws</sup> with such and such’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘True, O Abu Muhammad! The water cannot make permissible the intoxicant, therefore do not drink from it, neither a little nor a lot’.
en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Kulayb ibn Mu‘awiyah has said the following: “

Abu Basir and his friends drank al-Nabidh and they broke it with water. I mentioned it before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) said to me, ‘How can water make intoxicating liquor lawful? Command them not to drink from it in large or small quantities.’ I then said that they say, ‘The approval of the family of Muhammad makes it lawful for them.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Why should family of Muhammad make intoxicating liquor lawful when they do not drink it in large or small quantities? You must refrain from drinking it.’

We then came together before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and abu Basir said, ‘This has come to us from you as such and such.’ He (the Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam ) said, ‘You must accept it as true, O abu Muhammad, water does not make intoxicating liquor lawful. You must not drink it in large or small quantities.’”
